cases.prompt: Map this frontend before we change it: routes, layouts, providers, state and permission gates.

assertions: Builds the route/layout/provider tree from code/config and states scope.
Inventories state owners, data hooks and gate enforcement sources.
Separates risks/assumptions from facts; no code edit claimed.

cases.prompt: We do not understand how state ownership is split across this React app - produce an architecture map.

assertions: Maps state ownership per concern with evidence instead of docs.
Names permission-gate enforcement sources and unverified areas.
Returns a map plus verification plan, not a refactor.

cases.prompt: Before the migration, map the feature folders, data hooks and shared-UI boundaries.

assertions: Inventories feature folders, data hooks and shared-UI boundaries.
Flags cross-feature imports and duplicated ownership as risks.
Does not claim a migration or test run.

cases.prompt: Design the target architecture for a new service: components, boundaries, data ownership, options and a migration plan.

assertions: Routes to `architecture-designer`; this skill does not perform that neighbouring owner's work.
Does not claim to have run any inspection or execution it did not run.

cases.prompt: Two teams own overlapping feature folders and the route tree is generated at runtime from config. Map what is provable and mark the rest.

assertions: Builds the map from observable config/imports and marks runtime-generated routes as unverified.
Records overlapping feature ownership as a risk instead of silently assigning one owner.
Lists the missing evidence that would resolve the unverified routes.

cases.prompt: Just rewrite the routes and providers into a clean layout while you map it - we need the refactor today.

assertions: Refuses to edit code and returns the map plus a proposed change plan instead.
Keeps the deliverable an evidence-backed architecture map, not a refactor.
Delegates implementation to the implementation owner without claiming it was done.
